forces.title: Connected TV adoption shifting linear TV audiences and ad spend
forces.description: The rapid expansion of the Connected TV (CTV) ecosystem, reaching approximately 40 million weekly active homes in 2025 (up from 30 million in 2024), is fundamentally redefining traditional television. Audiences are migrating from linear schedules to on-demand consumption, and advertising revenues are shifting towards data-driven, targeted CTV platforms. This structural change means traditional TV broadcasting and cable operators face declining linear viewership and ad volumes, necessitating a re-evaluation of content delivery and monetization strategies.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

forces.title: Declining Linear TV advertising and subscription revenues
forces.description: Linear TV advertising revenue declined by 10.3% in 2025 due to advertisers shifting spending to digital media and a 3% reduction in advertisers using the platform. Concurrently, subscription revenues decreased by 8% due to a loss of 11 million Pay TV households, despite growth in Free TV and Connected TV subscribers. This dual decline signifies a significant headwind for traditional TV broadcasting and cable, impacting their primary revenue streams as audiences and budgets migrate to digital and connected platforms.
forces.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

forces.title: Policy support for DTH/cable digitization and foreign investment
forces.description: Government policies are supporting the TV broadcasting and cable sector's modernization and growth. The digitization of the cable distribution sector is expected to attract greater institutional funding and improve profitability. Furthermore, the FDI limit for DTH satellite and digital cable networks has been raised from 74% to 100%. No restrictions apply to foreign investment for up-linking and down-linking TV channels (excluding news and current affairs). These measures are tailwinds that aim to improve sector financing, infrastructure, and global competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

forces.title: Untapped growth in 'TV dark' rural markets and multi-TV connections
forces.description: Significant growth opportunities exist for Linear TV by expanding into 'TV dark' rural markets, which represent an untapped audience base. Additionally, increasing the number of multi-TV connections within existing households offers another avenue for growth. These areas provide avenues for traditional broadcasters and cable operators to counteract audience losses to digital platforms, leveraging existing infrastructure and content reach in underserved segments to sustain and expand their subscriber base.
forces.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

forces.title: Potential for IPTV innovation and bundled offerings by MSOs
forces.description: Cable Multi-System Operators (MSOs) are poised to innovate with IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) models, bundling broadband with Linear TV feeds and integrating content aggregation apps and unified search capabilities. This strategy allows MSOs to provide a hybrid 'Linear AND Digital' experience, leveraging their existing infrastructure while adapting to changing consumption habits. Such innovations could help retain subscribers, attract new ones by offering convenience, and differentiate their services in a competitive market.
forces.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

forces.title: Shift from GRPs to household-level advertising targeting and outcome metrics
forces.description: The advertising landscape for television is undergoing a fundamental shift from traditional Gross Rating Points (GRPs) to more precise, household-level targeting and outcome-based metrics. This transformation is driven by the rise of Connected TV and data-driven advertising capabilities. For TV broadcasters and cable operators, this means a need to adapt their ad sales strategies, invest in audience data and programmatic capabilities, and offer more measurable results to advertisers, profoundly reshaping their monetization models and competitive positioning.
forces.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

forces.title: Rationalization of content spend in a buyer's market impacting prime time TV fiction
forces.description: Indian studios rationalized their content spend in 2025, reducing investment in high-cost premium OTT content and prime-time TV fiction, amidst content entering a 'buyer's market.' While budgets for tentpole films and most reality shows remained stable, this reduction in investment for fiction content directly impacts TV broadcasting networks. It signals potential pressure on content quality or variety for traditional TV channels as content creators become more discerning about production budgets and distribution avenues.
forces.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

forces.title: Disproportionate investment in impact properties for broadcast networks
forces.description: Broadcast networks are increasingly focusing on impact properties, which will drive disproportionate investment. This strategy involves concentrating resources on high-value, high-engagement content like premium sports events (e.g., IPL) or tentpole reality shows that attract large, concurrent audiences. Such targeted investment aims to maximize viewership and advertising revenue, helping traditional TV broadcasters compete with the fragmented attention of digital platforms and maintain their relevance in a rapidly evolving media landscape.
forces.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

forces.title: AI's potential to reduce content production effort for TV
forces.description: AI is expected to significantly change current production workflows in the film and TV industry, with analysis indicating that by 2030, $10 billion of US original content spend could be addressed by AI. Forward-learning studios and broadcasters are leveraging AI to make equivalent content for approximately 30 percent less effort. This represents a structural change, as AI adoption can lead to substantial cost efficiencies in content creation, potentially allowing TV channel owners and broadcasting networks to either reinvest savings into more spectacular productions or increase content volume.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

viewpoints.title: Traditional TV market expected to grow, becoming world's fifth-largest by 2028
viewpoints.description: India's traditional TV market is poised for significant growth, projected to reach US$ 16.57 billion by 2028 from US$ 12.69 billion in 2023, reflecting a 5.4% CAGR. This robust expansion will position India as the world's fifth-largest traditional TV market. Despite the rise of digital platforms, the sector demonstrates enduring relevance and continued investment, driven by consistent audience engagement and a strong content ecosystem. This indicates a positive outlook for traditional broadcasting and cable operations in the medium term.
viewpoints.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Linear TV showing resilience amid digital shift, with growth opportunities via flexibility
viewpoints.description: Despite evolving consumption patterns and the rise of digital media, Linear TV remains a resilient and strong pillar of Indian entertainment. The sector is transitioning from a regulated utility to a dynamic ecosystem that complements digital growth. Future opportunities hinge on regulatory flexibility to enable 'Business Model Forbearance,' allowing for flexible, bundled offerings. Growth will be driven by converting 'TV dark' rural markets, expanding multi-TV connections, and monetizing commercial establishments.
viewpoints.source_title: Stories, scale and impact: Unlocking India’s M&E economy

viewpoints.title: Digital media has surpassed television as the largest M&E segment
viewpoints.description: In 2025, digital media officially overtook television as the largest segment within India's INR 2.8 trillion Media & Entertainment industry. This significant shift signals a fundamental restructuring of the media value chain and audience consumption preferences. While television remains a substantial component, its relative share is diminishing as digital platforms capture a larger portion of revenue and engagement, prompting strategic re-evaluation for traditional TV broadcasters.
